title: Pietro Chierico
text:
I am a biomedical engineer and PhD student working on digital health, physiological signal processing, wearable sensing, and AI-driven biomedical technologies.
My research focuses on photoplethysmography (PPG), cardiovascular monitoring, signal quality assessment, and reproducible biomedical AI.
I am affiliated with BioMIT.org at Universitat Politècnica de València and collaborate with Khalifa University on biomedical engineering and digital health research initiatives.

title: Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?
text:
Abstract
In a complete theory there is an element corresponding to each element of reality. A sufficient condition for the reality of a physical quantity is the possibility of predicting it with certainty, without disturbing the system. In quantum mechanics in the case of two physical quantities described by non-commuting operators, the knowledge of one precludes the knowledge of the other. Then either (1) the description of reality given by the wave function in quantum mechanics is not complete or (2) these two quantities cannot have simultaneous reality. Consideration of the problem of making predictions concerning a system on the basis of measurements made on another system that had previously interacted with it leads to the result that if (1) is false then (2) is also false. One is thus led to conclude that the description of reality as given by a wave function is not complete.

title: Research
text:
Current research directions

PPG signal quality assessment
I work on methods to detect and classify low-quality PPG segments in wearable monitoring. This is important because noisy signals can reduce the reliability of heart rate, pulse rate variability, blood pressure, and other physiological estimates.


Robust peak detection in PPG
I am interested in noise-resilient peak detection methods for PPG signals, especially for wearable and real-world monitoring conditions.


Reproducible biomedical AI
I am also interested in building biomedical AI methods that are transparent, reproducible, and useful for translational healthcare engineering.
